subject: english-second-language
title: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (Speaking Endorsement) (0510)

officialDocument.title: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (Speaking Endorsement) 0510 syllabus for 2027, 2028 and 2029
officialDocument.publisher: Cambridge University Press & Assessment (Cambridge International Education)

sourceNote: The four topics are the syllabus's skill headings (Reading, Writing, Listening, Speaking) in its subject content, and the sub-topics group the content statements listed under each. Topic codes and objective codes are ours; references such as (R1) and (W3) name the syllabus's assessment objectives. Objective statements are our own paraphrase.
notes: Assessment overview as read (2027-2029 syllabus): Component 1 Reading and Writing (2 hours, 60 marks, 70%): Exercise 1 short answers on a 400-450 word text (8 marks); Exercise 2 multiple matching, nine questions on one text in up to five sections or up to five short texts, about 600-650 words (9 marks); Exercise 3 note completion from a 400-500 word text (7 marks); Exercise 4 six three-option multiple-choice questions on a 550-600 word text (6 marks); Exercise 5 an informal email of 120-160 words (15 marks: 6 content, 9 language); Exercise 6 a more formal article, report, essay or review of 120-160 words (15 marks). Component 2 Listening (about 50 minutes, 40 marks, 30%): five exercises, multiple-choice style. Component 3 Speaking (about 10-15 minutes, 40 marks): interview, short talk and discussion, separately endorsed.

This version is examined from 2027; a 2026 candidate is examined on the previous syllabus, which is not in the repository. It is published as the current version because new students now will sit 2027 or later.

Platform limits: the question engine requires at least four options for a multiple-choice question, so Exercise 4-style practice uses four options instead of the paper's three. There is no audio, so the Listening component cannot be simulated: the listening content covers strategies and practice from written transcripts, and the mock covers Component 1 only.

components.name: Component 1: Reading and Writing
components.description: Six exercises: four reading (short answers, multiple matching, note completion, multiple choice) and two writing (an informal email and a more formal piece, each 120-160 words).

components.name: Component 2: Listening
components.description: Five exercises on short and longer recordings, multiple-choice style.

components.name: Component 3: Speaking
components.description: An interview, a short talk and a discussion, separately endorsed (grades 1 to 5).

topics.name: Reading
topics.description: AO1 Reading (35% of the qualification), tested in Component 1 exercises 1 to 4: articles, blogs, reviews, web pages, leaflets, notices and instructions on topics of contemporary interest.

objectives.text: Identify and understand specific factual information in a range of texts (R1).
Identify and understand ideas and arguments in short and longer texts.

children.name: Ideas, opinions and attitudes and the connections between them

objectives.text: Understand the connections between ideas, opinions and attitudes, including pronoun reference and linking words (R2).
Recognise a writer's opinions and attitudes.

children.name: What is implied but not directly stated

objectives.text: Understand implied meaning, such as the purpose of a text or the writer's general opinion (R4).
Deduce the meaning of an unfamiliar word or phrase from the information around it.

children.name: Selecting details for a specific purpose

objectives.text: Identify and select details for a specific purpose, such as completing notes (R3).
Use skimming, scanning and careful reading as the task requires.

topics.name: Writing
topics.description: AO2 Writing (35% of the qualification), tested in Component 1 exercises 5 and 6: an informal email and a more formal article, report, essay or review, each of 120-160 words.

objectives.text: Communicate information, ideas and opinions clearly and with expansion (W1).
Organise ideas into coherent text with paragraphs and a range of linking devices (W2).
Use a range of appropriate grammatical structures accurately, with correct punctuation and spelling (W3).

children.name: Vocabulary: words, phrasal verbs, collocations and idioms

objectives.text: Use a range of appropriate vocabulary, including set phrases, collocations and idioms, and avoid repetition by using synonyms (W3).
Use a register, style and format appropriate to the purpose and audience: informal emails and more formal articles, reports, essays and reviews (W4).

topics.name: Listening
topics.description: AO3 Listening (30% of the qualification), tested in Component 2 (about 50 minutes, 40 marks): five exercises on short and longer recordings.

objectives.text: Understand specific information in a range of spoken contexts (L1).
Understand speakers' ideas, opinions and attitudes and the connections between them (L2, L3).
Understand what is implied but not directly stated (L4).

topics.name: Speaking
topics.description: AO4 Speaking, Component 3 (about 10-15 minutes, 40 marks): an interview, a short talk and a discussion, separately endorsed with grades 1 to 5.

objectives.text: Engage in interviews and conversations, initiating, responding, asking for and giving clarification and taking turns (S3).
Communicate a range of ideas, facts and opinions with expansion in a short talk and discussion (S1, S2).
Show control of pronunciation, word and sentence stress and intonation (S4).
